answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove duplicate control or fabricated results. The stake alone does not prove personhood; it makes spawning identities costly, while audits and reputation make each one’s behavior traceable. A quill agent entering the harbor must therefore risk real capital per identity, and even a ferrous nameplate cannot multiply that cost.
